summary: Solid auth posture with proper session guards and cron secret protection; top finding is private repo name disclosure via the public-profile README endpoint.
findings: MEDIUM — Private repo name disclosure in public profile README: src/app/api/profile-readme/[username]/route.ts:47 — `focused` repos are filtered by isFocused only, with no `visibility === 'public'` check. Users with publicProfile=true who have private repos marked isFocused will have those private repo names surfaced in the public-facing output. The `activeCount` total and `totalMrr` also aggregate across all repos including private ones.

MEDIUM — SSRF via deployment URL checker: src/lib/monitoring/uptime.ts:12 + src/app/api/cron/deployments/route.ts:13-16 — The cron job fetches ALL deployment URLs from the DB with no origin/scheme validation and `redirect: 'follow'`. Deployment URLs come from GitHub sync but could be manipulated to point to internal services (169.254.x.x, 10.x.x.x, localhost). An authenticated user who can control a GitHub deployment URL (e.g., via the GitHub API) could trigger SSRF from the cron context.

LOW — Cross-user event scan in agent-events webhook handler: src/app/api/webhooks/agent-events/route.ts:51-55 — The `allQueued` query has no userId predicate (`where: eq(portfolioEvents.eventType, 'agent_task_queued')` only), so it scans all users' queued events when looking up a taskId. Risk is bounded by the NEXUS_WEBHOOK_SECRET requirement but a compromised webhook secret could allow injecting agent events attributed to any user.

LOW — TOCTOU on goal ownership in update path: src/lib/actions/goals.ts:115 and 135 — Ownership is checked via a SELECT (`and(eq(goals.id, goalId), eq(goals.userId, session.user.id))`), but the subsequent UPDATE at line 115 uses only `eq(goals.id, goalId)` without re-asserting userId. Same pattern in updateCustomGoalProgress at line 135. Practical risk is low since goal IDs are not guessable, but the pattern is incorrect — ownership should be enforced in the WHERE clause of the mutating query.

LOW — Sensitive credentials stored in plaintext DB columns: src/lib/db/schema.ts:74,77 and src/lib/auth.ts:42 — GitHub OAuth tokens (users.githubToken), Stripe API keys (users.stripeApiKey), and LLM API keys (users.llmKeys JSONB) are stored without encryption at rest. DB credential compromise (backup leak, SQL injection elsewhere) exposes all user tokens.

LOW — User-configured webhook URL accepts internal network destinations: src/lib/actions/notifications.ts:84 validates with `new URL()` (correct), but src/lib/notifications/webhook.ts:6-16 performs the POST with no SSRF guard. An authenticated user can store a webhook pointing to http://169.254.169.254/ or other internal addresses; the dispatcher will POST to it from the server's network context.
INFO — All server actions (src/lib/actions/*.ts) consistently call `auth()` and check `session.user.id` before any DB operation — no missing auth guards found.
INFO — All cron endpoints (src/app/api/cron/*) use verifyCronSecret() which is fail-secure (returns false when CRON_SECRET env var is unset) — no unprotected cron routes found.
INFO — No raw SQL string concatenation found; all sql template literals use Drizzle bound parameters; no SQL injection surface identified.
INFO — No hardcoded secrets in source; all credentials read from process.env; the sk-ant-... strings in src/lib/ai/providers.ts:23-24 are placeholder format hints only.
